author: Yuanyue Dang,William Zheng
description:
Having marked its 99th anniversary on August 1, the People’s Liberation Army is now just one year away from its centenary goals, with its evolution highlighting the past, present and future of China’s military strategy. In the third part of a series, Yuanyue Dang and William Zheng examine how Beijing leans on Mao-era doctrines and anti-corruption drives to guarantee absolute party control over the armed forces.
In December 1929, then Communist revolutionary Mao Zedong led a pivotal meeting in...
title: From Mao to now: why China’s Communist Party is  intent on control over the military

author: Alyssa Chen
description:
A recent US executive order requires major arms manufacturers to trace their multi-tier supply chains and actively phase out Chinese rare earths, aiming to end years of reliance on cheap minerals from China.
Far from a radical policy shift, industry observers view the directive as a long-overdue enforcement crackdown designed to inflict short-term contractor pain for long-term national security gain.
While contractors face immediate hurdles to requalify suppliers and find non-Chinese...
title: Pain or gain? US moves to decouple its defence industry from China’s rare earths

author: Holly Chik
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping has honoured a veteran naval test pilot with a first-class merit award for defence science and technology.
The pilot, Yang Yong, who had previously been awarded seven second- and third-class merit awards, has been testing planes launched from the country’s most advanced aircraft carrier, the Fujian.
Yang featured in a documentary that aired this week on state broadcaster CCTV and described a life-threatening incident in which his plane lost pressure at an altitude of...
title: Chinese test pilot who landed plane safely after cabin leak given first-class merit award

author: Seong Hyeon Choi
description:
The People’s Liberation Army (PLA) carried out a missile test in the Pacific last month.
The July 6 launch – in which a dummy warhead travelled 8,000km (5,000 miles) – was China’s first confirmed submarine-based missile test since 1982, and the first known firing from a nuclear-powered submarine.
The type of missile used has not been officially confirmed, but a report in the Global Times – a newspaper owned by the party mouthpiece People’s Daily – suggested it was a JL-3, which can be fired from...
title: Why China’s JL-3 made waves with first submarine-based missile test in over 40 years

author: Caroline Lin
description:
As China’s era of catch-up growth fades, experts warn that profound issues in research culture and institutional incentives may hamstring the country’s ambition to become a leader in scientific innovation.
In a dialogue held at the Shanghai Academy of Natural Sciences (SANS) last month, leading scholars discussed the hurdles China faces with Kevin Kelly, the founding executive editor of Wired magazine.
Lu Bai, a neurobiologist and the president of SANS, noted that China had been able to use...
title: As China’s catch-up era ends, what’s standing in the way of tech innovation?

author: Dannie Peng
description:
After a successful trial at a substation, China plans to expand the application of quantum technologies – including precision sensors and computer simulations – across its power grid to help prevent blackouts.
During the 18-month trial in Hefei in Anhui province, quantum technology was used to rapidly detect and diagnose equipment defects and faults in the power system, according to a report published on Wednesday by the party mouthpiece People’s Daily.
Quantum technology harnesses the physics...
title: China hopes to banish blackouts as quantum tech puts power grid in superposition

author: Holly Chik,Carol Yang
description:
The Chinese military held joint naval and air drills near Scarborough Shoal, a disputed reef in the South China Sea, on Saturday.
The training exercise came after Beijing hit out at the Philippines for an “illegal” attempt to extend its seabed rights off the coast of Palawan and map out its claims to the reef.
“This is a necessary action taken in light of the current situation in the South China Sea and in response to the acts of certain countries within the region that have undermined regional...
title: PLA stages South China Sea drills days after ‘illegal’ Philippine territorial bid

author: Lawrence Chung
description:
A political row is threatening to undermine Taiwan’s efforts to increase its stockpiles of military drones and has raised questions about the future of its domestic manufacturers.
On Monday, lawmakers failed to agree on competing versions of a bill to buy and develop military drones after six hours of debate.
While the ruling Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) and the opposition broadly agree on the need to expand the island’s arsenal of drones, they disagree about who should oversee the...
title: Taiwan’s political parties deadlocked over efforts to boost military drone capacity

author: Sophie Wushuang Yi
description:
As the Philippines hosted Southeast Asian foreign ministers in late July, the sea would not stay quiet. On July 20, Chinese and Philippine crews fought beside the BRP Sierra Madre with oars and batons; one Filipino sailor was reportedly injured while each side blamed the other.
Days later, with Foreign Minister Wang Yi and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio at the security forum, Philippine vessels went to the Scarborough Shoal. Manila said Chinese ships used water cannons on Philippine ships,...
title: To reduce South China Sea friction, Beijing and Manila need it in writing

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
As the People’s Liberation Army marks its 99th anniversary on August 1, one year from the deadline for its centenary goals, its evolution highlights the past, present and future of China’s military strategy. In the second part of a series, Gabriel Dominguez examines how Beijing is pushing the envelope on its near-seas island arc.
Beijing has urged the People’s Liberation Army to transform into a “world-class military” by the mid-21st century, intent on piercing US-led chokepoints along an arc of...
title: The numbers game: why the US is losing ground to China in the first island chain
